constraints: This is isolated static analysis of supplied evidence. No setup, import, API call, filesystem action or documented workflow is executed.
The super-entry selects an independent public invocation, module evaluation or analyst-owned analysis workflow. Its routing is analytical structure, not a TypeScript entrypoint-name dispatcher.
Omitted arguments remain distinct from explicit values. JavaScript parameter and destructuring defaults apply only to undefined; source truthiness tests retain their actual semantics.
Every call boundary consumes its displayed actual arguments. Normal outputs are actual callee returns after normal completion, never API content synthesized from request parameters.

Internal client-getter boundaries read the selected live binding at each call. A truthy binding returns its existing handle; otherwise current settings are validated, invalid settings throw before client/API acquisition, and successful construction uses a subsequent settings read and updates only the selected binding. Existing handles retain creation-time credential provenance.

Property, site, date-default and save-metadata settings reads remain independent of settings captured by a client handle. Earlier successful calls can affect later live bindings, including calls in the same analysis.

Report, Search Console, realtime, metadata, indexing and inspection call summaries below retain their respective request, projection, optional-save and return semantics. Their source bodies are also represented as independently callable capabilities.

Each saveResult boundary consumes the displayed actual data, category, operation and optional extra argument. It reads current settings, conditionally creates the category directory, constructs a separate metadata/data wrapper, serializes it, writes with replace semantics and returns the path. API and orchestration callers discard that path and return their response/result version.

Unless an actual catch is represented, any exception terminates that invocation and prevents later instructions. Preparation failure may precede a request; API failure follows an attempted request; save failure follows successful acquisition and may leave earlier writes intact.
Collection headers branch on has_member of their actual collection. True bodies obtain only the current member; backedges return to the header. Repeated members remain repeated work.

The analyst workflow implements source obligations from SKILL.md:53-64 at a distinct responsibility boundary. Supplied TypeScript does not automatically read analysis JSON or generate/write Markdown summaries.
Automatic saving remains a Skill obligation alongside implementation branches that disable or bypass saving. Neither source is silently assigned precedence over the other.
No analysis result, discarded saved path, filename, timestamp, operation label or current-property metadata establishes ownership of independently selected saved JSON.

Package declarations and lock entries are evidence of supplied versions, not an installation: @google-analytics/data ^4.9.0 / 4.12.1; @googleapis/indexing ^6.0.1 / 6.0.1; @googleapis/searchconsole ^6.0.1 / 6.0.1; dotenv ^16.4.7 / 16.6.1; googleapis ^170.0.0 / 170.1.0; tsx ^4.19.2 / 4.21.0; TypeScript ^5.7.2 / 5.9.3. The package is ESM and requires Node >=18.
import_module identifies the actually imported source module, with the selected export available from that module. High-level functions require index.ts.
Module evaluation uses entrypoint='moduleEvaluation'. Workflow-specific values belong to the analyst's context, not invented TypeScript function parameters.
The supplied evidence does not resolve workflow-selected paths, their ownership, the results-root anchor or a summary filename.
